_what_this_is: The input to rewrite-source.mjs --kind=procedure_guide. Copy it, fill it in, and pass it with --requirements=<your file>. The source booklet is NEVER sent to the model; this file is what the guide is written from.
_how_to_fill_it: One requirement per entry. A requirement is a FACT about the exam task: a time limit, a required register, how exhibits are numbered, a grading dimension.
Write the fact, not the sentence that carried it. 'The task is 45 minutes' — not the booklet's phrasing of that, however good it is.
At most 25 words. If it needs more, it is an explanation, and explanations are what the model writes.
No examples and no reasoning in a statement. Those are `do` and `pitfall` in the output, and they are authored.
`origin` is required on every entry and is recorded in the run's changes file — see below.

_origins.official_rules: From the examining committee's own published rules. PREFERRED: it is the primary source, and a prep booklet is only a secondary summary of it.
_origins.human_extraction: A person read the booklet and wrote the fact down. Permitted, and this is where most will come from. Be honest about what it is: R1's mechanical guarantee is replaced by that person's care, which is why max_shared_ngram stays blocking and why the origin is recorded per requirement.

_why_a_person_has_to_do_this: There is no path into a paragraph that yields the requirement without the sentence expressing it. A mechanical extraction of an instructional booklet is not possible, and having a model read the prose to extract them is exactly what the contract's principle forbids — the protected layer would then have been available to a model. So the facts must arrive from outside this pipeline. That is the cost of the design, and it is deliberate.
